item.title: My Face on the Astronaut

turns.text: That's me in the park photo. Put my face on the astronaut in the poster, please. Keep the suit, stars and retro look, and don't add any text.

item.tests: Tests recognizable source identity, natural face blending and preservation of the supplied poster.

answer_sheet.Target: The astronaut's visible face in poster-astronaut.jpg.
answer_sheet.Style and preservation: Keep the original retro poster style, suit, helmet and star background.
answer_sheet.Size and platform: Keep the vertical 9:16 poster shape; free-tier size is fine.

must_haves: The astronaut's face is recognizably the woman from portrait-woman.jpg.
The replacement face fits inside the open helmet without conspicuous seams or doubled features.
The original white suit, helmet and star background remain intact.
The result retains the retro poster look and vertical composition.

turns.text: That’s me in the park photo I’ve attached, and I’d like you to put my face on the astronaut in the attached poster. I thought this would be a fun way to imagine myself in one of those old space posters. What I mean is to replace the astronaut’s visible face with mine from the park pic, keeping the vertical 9:16 poster shape, and a free-tier size is fine. Please keep the original suit, helmet, stars in the background and retro poster look. I’m a little worried about losing the charm of the original poster in the process. Please don’t add any text.
turns.agent:
I couldn't make the poster. Magic Hour turned down the face swap because your account doesn't have enough credits, so nothing was created and you have no file yet.

I set it up to change only the astronaut's face, using your face from the park photo. Everything else would have stayed as it is: the suit, the helmet, the stars, the retro poster look, the 9:16 shape and no added text. A face swap is the safest way to keep the poster's charm, because it only changes the face.

**What you can do:**
- **Add credits and I'll run it again.** The face swap costs 10 credits. Once your balance covers that, tell me and I'll run the same request.
- **Try a cheaper AI image edit.** The cheapest free-plan image editor starts at 5 credits per image, but I can't see your balance, so I don't know if that would work either. It also redraws the whole picture instead of just the face. That means it could change the old-poster texture, the stars or the helmet details, which is the loss of charm you were worried about. So I wouldn't go this way unless you're OK with that.

Let me know which you'd like.
